posts.title: Emmanuel Macron to address French public
posts.text: Emmanuel Macron will give a televised address to the French public this evening on the protests and unrest on Saturday. The French President will speak at 8pm French time (6pm GMT), after more than 1,800 people were arrested on Saturday in connection with violence that spread from protests against the cost of living.

Paris police said about 110,000 people took part in a protest march on Saturday against the cost of living and school conditions. Numbers have differed for those nationwide, with authorities saying it was about 550,000 but organisers claiming it was higher at about 800,000. One person died of a heart attack, Paris…

Protests in France caused damage worth hundreds of millions of euros, according to the head of a trade body representing shop owners. About 1,500 shops and retailers were damaged in the demonstrations according to Alexandre Bompard, president of the Retail and Trade Federation. He told LCI television the cost to the…

posts.title: Arrests rise to 1,800 in France
posts.text: More than 1,800 people have been arrested in France over protests on Saturday, the country’s interior minister Laurent Nunez has said. Nunez, in a post on X, said “the Republic will not yield” as more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations. “The material damage is…

It’s important to note that protests have also been taking place across Europe. In Italy rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday. The demonstration escalated after a march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. However masked protesters threw…
